item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q017_prp8_evolutionary_mosaic","answer":"SCOPe’s decomposition of the Prp8 chain in PDB 3jb9 treats Prp8 as an evolutionary mosaic, not as one giant globular domain with a single history. The structured core is split into five separately classified domains: four can be related to folds or superfamilies that were already known from other proteins, while one Prp8-specific domain was classified as a newly observed fold. The recognizable pieces are the reverse-transcriptase-like domain, consistent with the proposed relationship between Prp8 and group-II-intron reverse transcriptase/maturase proteins; an RNase-H-like domain; a restriction-endonuclease/RuvC-like nuclease domain; and the C-terminal Jab1/MPN-like domain related to JAMM/MPN metalloprotease folds. Those assignments support ancient domain-level ancestry or fold reuse, but they should not be read as whole-chain homology to any one of those enzymes, nor as automatic transfer of reverse-transcriptase, RNase H, endonuclease, or JAMM protease activity, because Prp8 uses several of these domains as degenerate spliceosomal scaffolding and regulatory modules with missing or altered catalytic motifs. The remaining Prp8 linker/insert domain is the SCOPe new-fold case: it should be represented and modeled as its own Prp8 fold rather than being forced into the RT, RNase-H, endonuclease, or Jab1/MPN families.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
